search_log: Searched "The 6:20 Man" "David Baldacci" official excerpt and first chapter; found the Hachette-affiliated audio page and a substantial Chapter 1–2 excerpt reproduced by Colloquium.
Searched "The 6:20 Man" point of view, third person, and narrator; found BookRags' explicit whole-book description of third-person limited narration.
Searched for multiple narrators, alternating point of view, epistolary structure, and frame narrative; found no credible indication of sustained narration in another grammatical person.

Checked Google Books and Open Library/Internet Archive discovery results; accessible Google Books content was descriptive, and the Open Library page timed out, so neither supplied usable narrative-person evidence.
Targeted searches for Chapter 1 and interior Devine passages found third-person prose but also unauthorized full-text mirrors, which were not used as evidence.
person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages present the focal character externally as he while allowing access to his perceptions, consistent with third-person limited narration. Universal or conversational I, we, and you instances occur in speech, aphorisms, or free-indirect generalization and do not establish first- or second-person base narration. BookRags explicitly characterizes the whole novel as third person limited to Travis Devine, and the substantial opening excerpt independently demonstrates that pattern. No credible evidence of alternating or framed first-person sections was found. Confidence is medium because the explicit whole-book source is Tier C and the corroborating prose excerpt covers only the opening.
